basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Represents money as an exact decimal amount with a currency code pinned to a catalogue edition, never as a binary float.
Requires a named rule for every rounding and exposes the residual it creates.
Keeps conversion separate: rates are chosen by a caller policy and recorded with the result.
Leaves display formatting to locale data and payments to financial message models.

may: Parse and normalize an exact decimal amount.
Validate a currency code against the pinned catalogue edition.
Allocate a total into parts that reconcile exactly.
Calculate a reproducible conversion under a declared rate.
mustNot: Store or compute monetary amounts in binary floating point.
Add or compare amounts in different currencies without a declared conversion.
Round without a named rule or hide the rounding residual.
Pick an exchange rate without recording its source and time.
Initiate a payment or transfer of funds.
requiresHuman: Choosing the rate policy for a binding financial conversion.
Approving changes to rounding rules that affect customer charges.

considerations: Rounding and conversion errors can systematically overcharge customers or underpay workers.
Prices and fees shown must match what is charged.
Historic and redenominated currencies need care so old debts and benefits are valued fairly.

items: A monetary value is an exact decimal amount with an ISO 4217 code and optional valuation context.
Often confused with a price, a balance and a formatted display string.
Currency mix-ups multiply or divide amounts wrongly.
Untraceable rates make conversions impossible to audit.
